blogs.title: The Exemptive Timeframe: How 'Pending' Proceedings Survive Two Decades of FOIA Litigation
blogs.description: This post analyzes the D.C. Circuit's resolution of the 'pending or reasonably anticipated' requirement for Exemption 7(A) in cases involving long-term counterterrorism investigations. It dissects the court's reliance on updated agency declarations (Hardy/Bender) to sustain secrecy after the initial immigration proceedings began in 2002, and how the 'context counsels against isolation' standard alters the FOIA burden of proof in temporal disputes.

blogs.title: Ex Parte Evidence in the D.C. Circuit: The Trust Required to Seal the Public Record
blogs.description: Focusing on the procedural mechanisms used in litigation to protect sensitive law enforcement information, this post examines the D.C. Circuit's willingness to rely on ex parte declarations to resolve disputes over both enforcement pendency and document segregability. It explores the tension between judicial transparency requirements and the 'intrinsic' nature these declarations are highlighted as being 'unavoidable' in cases where the disputed material is the secret itself.

blogs.title: Information vs. Ink: Applying the 'Mead Data' 'Reasonable Segregation' Standard to Massive Investigative Files
blogs.description: This technical analysis breaks down the application of the *Mead Data* standard to a 10,750-page FBI file, specifically the 'information, not simply words' prohibition on segregable material. It assesses why the 'interspersed line-by-line' prohibition on disclosure leads courts to deny total withholding credibility, and what the 'no meaningful information' threshold means for practitioners requesting freedom of information.
